candidates.question: What system or tool is currently used to check room availability and record the reservation — for example, a calendar application, a dedicated room booking portal, or a manual spreadsheet?
What system or method does the organizer use to check room availability and submit the reservation request?
What specific inputs must be provided before a reservation can be made — such as meeting date, start and end time, expected number of attendees, or required equipment?
Is any approval or confirmation required from a facility manager or administrator before the reservation is considered confirmed?
When multiple rooms are available for the requested time slot, what criteria determine which room is selected?
What happens when the requested room is unavailable for the desired time slot — does the organizer manually search for alternatives, or is an alternative automatically suggested?
What happens when no suitable room is available for the requested time — is the meeting rescheduled, moved to an alternative location, or escalated to someone for resolution?
How is room information communicated to participants — for example, through a calendar invitation, a separate email, or a messaging platform — and is this step performed manually or automatically?
How is the confirmed room information communicated to participants — for example, through a calendar invite update, an email notification, or a message in a team chat tool?
What is the process if the organizer needs to cancel or change the reservation after it has been confirmed?
Approximately how many room reservations are made per day or per week, and is there a predictable peak period when demand is highest?
Are there any steps that must be completed after the meeting ends, such as formally releasing the room or recording that it was used?
